_comment: 24/7 inpatient hospital -- distinct from the outpatient `clinic` type, which closes overnight (see clinic/schedule.json). occupancy_fraction is Ahmed, Akhondzada, Kurnitski & Olesen (2017, Sustainable Cities and Society 35:134-144, Table 6 'Hospital' column) -- REHVA Technology and Research Committee-collected national schedule data feeding the prEN16798-1/ISO 17772-1 standards, the only source in this repo's usual reference set with a Hospital-specific (as opposed to generic office/school) occupancy schedule. Its never-fully-zero day-shape (0.4 overnight baseline, 0.8 daytime peak, weekday > weekend during business hours) independently matches the real hospital's design occupancy schedule in Dobosi, Tanasa, Kaba, Retezan & Mihaila (2019, E3S Web of Conferences 111, 06073) Figure 5 -- two independent sources agreeing on shape. heat_gain_present_kw (0.118 kW) is that same Ahmed et al. Table 4 'Hospital' row's average total (sensible+latent) heat loss per occupant (118.3 W at M=1.2 met, A_DU=1.80 m^2, Du Bois formula) -- a hospital-specific ISO 7730/Fanger-model figure, unlike most other types here which fall back to a generic ~0.100 kW ballpark. gain_w_per_m2 (13 W/m^2) is that Table 5 row's lighting (9.0) + appliances (4.0) unit-load figures (same source, same table family). heat_gain_active_kw, active_fraction, and asleep_probabilities have no equivalent in Ahmed et al. (it models one occupant count only, no active/asleep split) -- illustrative choices of this repo's own, same 'not survey-calibrated' caveat as every other type's non-cited fields. asleep_probabilities gives genuine overnight n_asleep output (inpatients sleep) through the same mechanism as hotel -- see core/occupancy_engine.py module docstring. Uses hourly_occupancy_curve (like hotel), not fixed_schedule, because a hospital has no single open/close window: inpatients are present around the clock.
description: 24/7 inpatient hospital. Continuous occupancy (inpatients, round-the-clock staff) with a daytime peak (rounds, scheduled procedures, admin, visiting hours) over an overnight baseline; unlike the outpatient `clinic` type, never closes.
